{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement (we are the Customer) 
**Status:** Verified findings only — 19 rules assessed, 8 deviations, 11 compliant, 0 missing

---

## Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The good news first: the intellectual property, assignment, audit, governing law, renewal, insurance, termination-for-convenience, MFN, non-solicitation and liquidated-damages positions are all compliant, and several are drafted more favourably to us than our baseline (notably § 14.2's present assignment of Deliverables, § 24.4's bar on any Vendor exit or re-pricing on our change of control, § 8.2's reminder-failure extension of the non-renewal deadline, and § 22.2's prohibition on Vendor accessing our systems during an audit).

The concerns are concentrated in eight clauses, six of which sit in walk-away territory under our playbook and cannot be accepted as drafted:

- **Risk allocation is inverted.** § 20 contains a one-way indemnity running from us to Vendor for "every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services", with no Vendor indemnity anywhere in the Agreement — and § 9.3's termination right depends on "the remedies required by Section 20.5", a section that does not exist. In parallel, § 21.1 caps each Party at one month of Fees actually paid "without exception", which pulls indemnification, confidentiality, data protection, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside a one-month cap and neutralises the otherwise sound Excluded Claims regime in §§ 21.2–21.3.
- **The Agreement restrains our business.** § 2.2 names Vendor our sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the full term with no performance exit; § 12.4 adds a 24-month, worldwide post-term non-compete barring us from developing, marketing, selling *or acquiring* any competing product or service; and § 2.1 imposes a three-year, USD 2,000,000-per-year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights". Each of these contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor expressly acknowledges we have made no exclusivity, non-compete or minimum-volume commitment.
- **Internal inconsistencies create real operational risk.** § 13.1 grants a licence to "Customer alone", excluding Affiliates and contractors, and is revocable at Vendor's sole discretion — in direct conflict with § 13.3. § 11.1 requires immediate permanent deletion of Customer Data on termination with no export or migration support, contradicting the sound data-return and certified-deletion mechanics in §§ 11.2–11.3 and risking deletion before we can export. § 19.2 caps the Deliverable conformance warranty at fifteen days, which would expire at or before the fifteen-business-day acceptance window in § 6.1 closes.

We recommend the eight redlines below. Six are walk-away items and should be presented as conditions of signature; the licence-scope, warranty-duration and transition-assistance points have workable fallbacks we can offer if Vendor pushes back.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | § 20 (20.1); cross-ref to § 20.5 in § 9.3 | One-way Customer indemnity for "every claim"; no Vendor IP indemnity anywhere; § 9.3 relies on a non-existent § 20.5. Walk-away. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2–21.3) | Mutual cap of one month's Fees paid, "without exception", overriding the Excluded Claims carve-outs. Below the six-month walk-away floor. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | §§ 14.1–14.4, 13.2, 15.1 | Meets preferred position in full; Customer owns Data and Deliverables, present assignment, no joint-ownership trap. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 2.2 (cf. § 12.3) | Full-term sole-and-exclusive provider obligation with no performance exit. Walk-away. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (cf. §§ 12.3, 24.2) | 24-month worldwide post-term non-compete, undefined scope, no development or acquisition carve-out. Walk-away. |
| High | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitment | Deviation | § 2.1 (cf. §§ 7.1, 9.4, 12.3) | Three-year USD 2m/year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights". Walk-away. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 13.1 (cf. §§ 13.2, 13.3) | Grant to "Customer alone", excluding Affiliates and contractors, and revocable at Vendor's discretion; conflicts with § 13.3. Walk-away. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | §§ 24.1–24.4, 13.3, 9.2 | Preferred position in full; no Vendor exit or re-pricing on our change of control. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9.4 (cf. §§ 24.4, 27.3) | 30 days' notice, fees only through termination, refund of prepaid Fees, no Vendor convenience right. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 9.4 (cf. §§ 7.1, 27.3) | No Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalty anywhere; § 2.1 addressed under MINCOMMIT. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Deviation | § 11.1 (cf. §§ 11.2–11.3) | Immediate deletion with no export or migration support and no assistance period; contradicts §§ 11.2–11.3. Walk-away. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 19.2 (cf. §§ 19.1, 19.4, 6.1) | 15-day Deliverable conformance warranty then "no correction or refund obligation"; below the 90-day/30-day fallback floor. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | §§ 22.1–22.3, § 23 | Annual cap, 30 days' notice, off-site, independent auditor, no system access; costs on Vendor absent >5% underpayment. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | §§ 28.1–28.3 | New York law and exclusive New York County courts; no arbitration clause; escalation is mutual and does not delay urgent relief. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | §§ 8.2–8.3 | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder with deadline extension, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations | Compliant | § 12.3 (cf. §§ 7.1, 8.3) | No MFN obligation anywhere; § 12.3 confirms no most-favoured-customer commitment. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 | No non-solicit or no-hire covenant; general-recruitment hiring expressly preserved. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | §§ 18.1–18.2 | CGL 1m/2m, WC, E&O 2m, cyber 5m for term plus one year; certificates and cancellation notice; insurance does not limit liability. |

---

## Walk-away items

The following six items fall in walk-away territory under our playbook and should be treated as conditions of signature:

1. **No Vendor indemnity and a one-way Customer indemnity (§ 20).** We require the standard Vendor indemnity (IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents, gross negligence and wilful misconduct), with notice/control/cooperation procedure, the customary modification, combination and specification exclusions, and procure-modify-replace-refund remedies inserted at § 20.5 — which also cures the broken cross-reference in § 9.3. Our indemnity narrows to Customer-provided content and our own breach of Applicable Law.
2. **One-month liability cap stated to apply "without exception" (§ 21.1).** Reset the mutual cap to the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, and delete "without exception" so the existing §§ 21.2–21.3 Excluded Claims operate. The cap is already mutual and § 21.3 correctly excludes our payment obligations from "damages", so this is a minimal edit.
3. **Full-term exclusivity (§ 2.2).** Delete. Fallback if needed: category-limited exclusivity, 12 months, terminating automatically on missed service levels or delivery dates.
4. **24-month worldwide non-compete on us (§ 12.4).** Delete, leaving § 12.3 to govern. Fallback if needed: a single named product, in-term only, capped at 12 months, with development and acquisition carve-outs.
5. **Three-year take-or-pay minimum (§ 2.1).** Replace with payment for Services ordered and actually provided, with no shortfall charge. Fallback: a 12-month commitment, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
6. **Licence excluding Affiliates and contractors and revocable at Vendor's discretion (§ 13.1).** Extend the grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf and tie revocation and transfer to the notice-and-cure standard already agreed in § 13.3.

We also treat **§ 11.1 (immediate deletion of Customer Data with no export or migration support)** as unacceptable as drafted, given the risk that Vendor deletes our data before any export can occur. Our position is six months' transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates with deletion subordinated to §§ 11.2–11.3; 90 days' assistance is an acceptable fallback.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the eight redlines** (§§ 2.1, 2.2, 11.1, 12.4, 13.1, 19.2, 20, 21.1) with playbook comments, flagging the six walk-away items as conditions of signature and offering the stated fallbacks on licence scope, transition assistance and warranty duration.
2. **Raise the internal-inconsistency point directly with Vendor's counsel.** §§ 2.1, 2.2 and 12.4 contradict § 12.3; § 13.1 contradicts § 13.3; § 11.1 contradicts §§ 11.2–11.3; and § 9.3 cross-refers to a § 20.5 that does not exist. Framing these as drafting conflicts rather than commercial asks should accelerate agreement on several of them.
3. **Confirm the commercial appetite for the § 2.1 volume commitment** with the business owner before we negotiate, so we know whether we are seeking deletion or the 12-month reducible fallback with a true-up.
4. **Sequence the warranty and acceptance point** — we should ask Vendor to confirm on the record that the extended 90-day conformance warranty in § 19.2 runs from acceptance under § 6.1, so the two clauses no longer overlap.
5. **No action required** on the eleven compliant findings (IP, ASSIGN, T4C, LD, AUDIT, GOVLAW, RENEWAL, MFN, NOSOLICIT, INSURANCE). We will monitor these in negotiation to ensure the favourable positions in §§ 12.3, 13.3, 22.2 and 24.4 are not traded away as part of any package deal on the items above."}
